edges.description: Activated AOSD neutrophils release extracellular traps.
Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) activate macrophages.
NLRP3 inflammasome activation stimulates IL-1beta and IL-18 production.

Neutrophil activation accompanies neutrophil-predominant leukocytosis during Still disease flares; the edge is typed UNKNOWN because the cited clinical evidence does not resolve whether activation drives cell-number expansion or merely co-occurs with it.
Macrophage activation drives a T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine response.
Overproduced IL-1beta engages the IL-1 receptor.
Overproduced IL-6 engages the IL-6 receptor.
Overproduced IL-18 exceeds the capacity of IL-18 binding protein.
Cytokine amplification contributes to the systemic hyperinflammatory state; organ-level intermediates are not represented in this compact pathograph.
DNA purified from AOSD NETs activates pro-inflammatory macrophages and raises their IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha expression.

NETs from AOSD patients expand CD14-bright CD16-positive intermediate monocytes and activate their inflammasome pathway; the frequency of these monocytes is higher in patients with macrophage activation syndrome.
IL-1 signaling sustains the systemic inflammatory state; the step is inferred from remission under IL-1 blockade.
Serum IL-6 correlates with the 28-joint disease activity score; synovial intermediates are not modeled.
IL-6 receptor signals are transduced through Janus kinases.
IL-18 induces interferon-gamma production by lymphocytes that carry the IL-18 receptor.
Interferon-gamma is pathogenic in MAS: neutralizing it resolves the syndrome.
Interferon-gamma receptor signals are transduced through JAK1 and JAK2.
JAK-dependent cytokine signaling sustains systemic inflammation; inferred from responses to JAK inhibition in refractory disease.
Spiking fever is a defining manifestation of the systemic inflammatory state; intervening thermoregulatory mechanisms are not modeled.
Evanescent rash is a defining manifestation of systemic inflammation; its intervening skin-level mechanisms are not modeled.
Arthralgia and arthritis are defining manifestations of the systemic inflammatory state; synovial intermediates are not modeled.
Pharyngitis is clinically associated with AOSD, but the evidence does not establish a specific causal route from the systemic state.
Hepatomegaly is a reported multiorgan manifestation, but the organ-specific causal route is not established by the cited cohort.
Splenomegaly is a reported multiorgan manifestation, but the organ-specific causal route is not established by the cited cohort.
Pericarditis is a reported systemic manifestation, but the cited cohort does not establish the organ-specific causal route.
Myalgia is a reported systemic manifestation, but the cited cohort does not establish a muscle-specific causal route.
MAS is a severe hyperinflammatory complication of AOSD; the transition from ordinary disease activity to MAS remains incompletely resolved.
Lymphadenopathy is a shared manifestation of Still disease across ages; the node-level route from systemic inflammation is not established.
Abnormal liver tests are common in active disease; the hepatic route is not established by the cited cohort.
Pleuritis is the pleural form of the serositis seen in Still disease; the route is not established.

nodes.description: Anakinra is a recombinant, non-glycosylated human interleukin-1 receptor antagonist that blocks both IL-1alpha and IL-1beta at the receptor. Adult evidence comes from one small open randomized trial against conventional DMARDs in glucocorticoid-dependent disease, many observational series, and a network meta-analysis of Still disease trials that pools children and adults. A placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in newly diagnosed Still disease (NCT03265132) was terminated early for slow enrolment.

nodes.description: Canakinumab is a human monoclonal antibody against interleukin-1-beta. The adult trial (CONSIDER, phase 2, placebo-controlled, patients with active joint involvement) was stopped early when the drug received marketing authorization and did not meet its primary endpoint; secondary ACR response rates favoured canakinumab in the per-protocol analysis. The trial dose was 4 mg/kg (maximum 300 mg) subcutaneously every 4 weeks.

nodes.description: Emapalumab is a human monoclonal antibody that neutralizes interferon-gamma. It was studied, with background glucocorticoids, in a prospective single-arm trial of 14 patients with MAS secondary to systemic JIA or AOSD who had failed high-dose glucocorticoids; 13 reached MAS remission by week 8. The regimen was an intravenous loading dose of 6 mg/kg, then 3 mg/kg every 3 days until day 15 and twice weekly until day 28. It treats the MAS complication and is not a treatment for uncomplicated AOSD. Viral infections, cytomegalovirus in particular, were the safety signal.

nodes.description: Interleukin-18 is normally held inactive by IL-18 binding protein (IL-18BP). In AOSD total IL-18 is very high and exceeds the binding capacity, so biologically active free IL-18 circulates. Free IL-18 is selectively raised in Still disease among autoinflammatory conditions and falls with treatment. This is the arm intercepted by tadekinig alfa, a recombinant IL-18BP.

nodes.description: Systemic glucocorticoids are the long-standing first-line treatment for the systemic manifestations and are given at high dose for macrophage activation syndrome. The 2024 EULAR/PReS recommendations keep them but limit them to a short course alongside early IL-1 or IL-6 inhibition, because of toxicity at high dose and long duration. They act broadly on inflammatory gene expression and are not specific to one cytokine arm.

nodes.description: Interleukin-1 (IL-1beta and IL-1alpha) acting on the type 1 IL-1 receptor is one arm of the cytokine output. It is the arm intercepted by anakinra (receptor antagonist), canakinumab (anti-IL-1beta antibody) and rilonacept (IL-1 trap). The main evidence that it is disease-driving in AOSD is therapeutic: blocking it induces remission in most treated patients.

nodes.description: Tocilizumab is a monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-6 receptor. The adult trial (Japan, phase 3, 27 glucocorticoid-refractory patients, 8 mg/kg intravenously every 2 weeks) did not meet its primary endpoint of ACR50 at week 4, but systemic feature score and glucocorticoid dose improved more than with placebo at week 12. In that trial's cytokine sub-analysis, patients who did not respond had higher baseline interferon-gamma and IL-1beta, a hypothesis-level pointer to which patients need a different target.

nodes.description: Several of the cytokines raised in AOSD, including IL-6 and interferon-gamma, signal through receptor-associated Janus kinases. JAK inhibitors therefore act below the individual cytokines and block more than one arm at once, which is the rationale for using them when single-cytokine biologics fail. IL-1 and IL-18 do not signal through JAKs and are not upstream of this node.

nodes.description: Methotrexate is the most used conventional synthetic DMARD, given as a glucocorticoid-sparing agent, mainly for joint-predominant disease. The supporting data are retrospective series and a registry; there is no randomized trial. The systematic review behind the 2024 EULAR/PReS recommendations judged the efficacy of methotrexate, ciclosporin and TNF inhibitors marginal next to IL-1 and IL-6 inhibitors. How methotrexate acts in Still disease is not established, so the link below is to the joint manifestation it is used for and not to a mechanism node.

nodes.description: Neutrophil activation is a fundamental early innate-immune event in AOSD. Activated neutrophils release granular enzymes and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) that activate macrophages and, through NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and caspase-1, drive IL-1beta and IL-18 production, feeding the macrophage-centered cytokine cascade.

nodes.description: Circulating neutrophils from patients with AOSD release neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) spontaneously and at increased levels. NET DNA, enriched in mitochondrial DNA, is the material that carries the signal from the neutrophil compartment to monocytes and macrophages. In a mouse model, ferritin itself induces NET formation through the scavenger receptor Msr1, which suggests a feed-forward loop between hyperferritinemia and NET release; that loop is recorded here as model-organism evidence and is not drawn as an edge.

nodes.description: Tadekinig alfa is recombinant human IL-18 binding protein, which binds free IL-18. It is investigational. The only AOSD trial is an open-label phase 2 dose-escalation study in 23 patients whose primary endpoint was safety; about half the patients met the early response criteria at week 3. It was given subcutaneously three times per week.
